/hr/gcr.io-k8s-staging-nfd-charts-node-f.title: node-feature-discovery helm release
/hr/gcr.io-k8s-staging-nfd-charts-node-f.name: node-feature-discovery
/hr/gcr.io-k8s-staging-nfd-charts-node-f.doc:
Node Feature Discovery is a Kubernetes add-on that helps automate the discovery and configuration of node features such as CPU, memory, and network interfaces.

Most people in k8s at home use Node Feature Discovery to ensure that pods that need video transcoding capabilities are running on a node with an Intel GPU (which has excellent video transcoding capabilities). But also for detecting a Zigbee/Z-Wave USB sticks.

For example, the following code would guarantee that a node will run on a Node with Intel GPU:

affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: feature.node.kubernetes.io/custom-intel-gpu
            operator: In
            values:
              - "true"

Node Feature Discovery, would figure out a node has an Intel GPU and add the feature.node.kubernetes.io/custom-intel-gpu: true label.

/hr/cloudflare.github.io-helm-charts-clo.title: cloudflared helm release
/hr/cloudflare.github.io-helm-charts-clo.name: cloudflared
/hr/cloudflare.github.io-helm-charts-clo.doc: Cloudflared is a lightweight proxy client for securely connecting applications to Cloudflare’s network. It powers Cloudflare Tunnel, allowing services to be exposed without opening ports or configuring firewall rules. cloudflared routes traffic through Cloudflare’s global network, enhancing security with DDoS protection, authentication, and encrypted connections. It supports HTTP, TCP, and QUIC, making it ideal for self-hosted services, remote access, and zero-trust networking.

set -euo pipefail
P=/opt/data/.local
# Keep one version per line so Renovate can find and bump them.
# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=cli/cli
GH=2.103.3
# renovate: datasource=golang-version depName=go
GO=1.27.3
# Homebrew keeps itself up to date once installed, so this
# only picks the version for a fresh install.
# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=Homebrew/brew
BREW=7.0.11
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64) A=amd64 ;;
  aarch64|arm64) A=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "unsupported architecture" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
mkdir -p "$P/bin"

# Reinstall whenever the installed version doesn't match the
# pin, and check every download against its published checksum.
INSTALLED_GH=$("$P/bin/gh" --version 2>/dev/null || true)
if [[ "$INSTALLED_GH" != "gh version $GH "* ]]; then
  G=gh_"$GH"_linux_"$A"
  C=gh_"$GH"_checksums.txt
  U="https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v$GH"
  curl -fsSLo "/tmp/$G.tar.gz" "$U/$G.tar.gz"
  curl -fsSL "$U/$C" | awk -v f="$G.tar.gz" '$2 == f' | (cd /tmp && sha256sum -c -)
  tar xOzf "/tmp/$G.tar.gz" "$G/bin/gh" >/tmp/gh
  install -o 10000 -g 10000 -m 755 /tmp/gh "$P/bin/gh"
  rm -f "/tmp/$G.tar.gz" /tmp/gh
fi

if [ "$(head -n1 "$P/go/VERSION" 2>/dev/null)" != "go$GO" ]; then
  T=go"$GO".linux-"$A".tar.gz
  curl -fsSLo "/tmp/$T" "https://dl.google.com/go/$T"
  echo "$(curl -fsSL "https://dl.google.com/go/$T.sha256")  /tmp/$T" | sha256sum -c -
  rm -rf "$P/.go"
  mkdir "$P/.go"
  tar xzf "/tmp/$T" -C "$P/.go" --strip-components=1
  rm -f "/tmp/$T"
  chown -R 10000:10000 "$P/.go"
  rm -rf "$P/go"
  mv "$P/.go" "$P/go"
fi

if [ ! -x "$P/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  rm -rf "$P/.homebrew" "$P/homebrew"
  git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$BREW" https://github.com/Homebrew/brew.git "$P/.homebrew"
  chown -R 10000:10000 "$P/.homebrew"
  mv "$P/.homebrew" "$P/homebrew"
fi

# Pin as a pair: mnemosyne-hermes declares a floor on
# mnemosyne-memory, not an exact pin, so a free uv pick can
# land a broken combination (0.7.0-0.7.2 + 3.x failed every
# memory tool call with an ImportError). 0.7.7 requires
# mnemosyne-memory>=4.0.0.
# renovate: datasource=pypi depName=mnemosyne-hermes
MNEMOSYNE_HERMES=0.7.7
# renovate: datasource=pypi depName=mnemosyne-memory
MNEMOSYNE_MEMORY=4.0.0
MNEMOSYNE_VENV="$P/mnemosyne"
if [ ! -x "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/python" ]; then
  uv venv --python /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV"
fi
if ! "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/python" -c "import importlib.metadata as m; assert m.version('mnemosyne-hermes') == '$MNEMOSYNE_HERMES'; assert m.version('mnemosyne-memory') == '$MNEMOSYNE_MEMORY'" 2>/dev/null; then
  # The hermes-agent image quarantines PyPI uploads for 14
  # days (exclude-newer in its bundled pyproject.toml), so
  # fresh mnemosyne releases cannot resolve for two weeks.
  # Deliberately bypassed here: both packages are exact-pinned
  # above, so the quarantine buys nothing for this install.
  UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER="0 days" uv pip install --python "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/python" --upgrade \
    "mnemosyne-hermes==$MNEMOSYNE_HERMES" \
    "mnemosyne-memory[embeddings]==$MNEMOSYNE_MEMORY"
fi

rm -rf /opt/data/plugins/mnemosyne
HERMES_HOME=/opt/data "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/mnemosyne-hermes" install \
  --mode wrapper \
  --python "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/python"
HERMES_HOME=/opt/data "$MNEMOSYNE_VENV/bin/mnemosyne-hermes" status
mkdir -p /opt/data/mnemosyne
chown -R 10000:10000 /opt/data/mnemosyne

set -eu
cp /desired/{config.yaml,SOUL.md} /staging/
touch /staging/.env /opt/data/.env
sed -i '/^[[:space:]]*API_SERVER_KEY[[:space:]]*=/d' /opt/data/.env
HERMES_HOME=/staging HOME=/staging /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python -c 'from hermes_cli.config import migrate_config; migrate_config(interactive=False,quiet=False)'
mkdir -p /opt/data/workspace
chown 0:0 /opt/data/workspace
chmod 750 /opt/data/workspace
chown 10000:10000 /opt/data/workspace
for f in config.yaml SOUL.md; do
  rm -f "/opt/data/.$f.new"
  install -m 600 "/staging/$f" "/opt/data/.$f.new"
  chown 10000:10000 "/opt/data/.$f.new"
  mv -f "/opt/data/.$f.new" "/opt/data/$f"
done
chown 0:0 /opt/data/.env 2>/dev/null || touch /opt/data/.env
chmod 600 /opt/data/.env
chown 10000:10000 /opt/data/.env

set -eu
cd /models
fetch() {
  name=$1 sha=$2 url=$3
  if [ -f "$name" ] && [ "$(cat "$name.sha256" 2>/dev/null)" = "$sha" ]; then
    return
  fi
  curl -fL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors -C - -o "$name.part" "$url"
  echo "$sha  $name.part" | sha256sum -c - || { rm -f "$name.part"; exit 1; }
  mv "$name.part" "$name"
  echo "$sha" > "$name.sha256"
}

/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.title: immich-microservices helm release
/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.name: immich-microservices
/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.doc:
Immich is a self-hosted photo and video backup solution.

For immich, there are multiple helm deployments:

  • immich-web
  • immich-server
  • immich-typesense
  • immich-machine-learning
  • immich-microservices (this one)

For redis and postgres, there are multiple helm charts:

  • Redis: app-template/redis, bitnami/redis
  • PostgreSQL: operator cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg, bitnami bitnami/postgresql
